messages.text: For a Semiconductor use case involving RFIC validation, where would Signaling / Non-signaling Tester fit in the test workflow?

In an RFIC validation workflow, **non-signaling test comes earlier and deeper at the RF/PHY characterization level**, while **signaling test comes later when the RFIC is integrated enough to behave like a real wireless device/system**.

Typical placement:

```text
1. Silicon bring-up / bench debug
   → Non-signaling tester, VSG/VSA, spectrum analyzer, network analyzer

2. RF parametric validation
   → Non-signaling tester
   → TX power, EVM, ACLR, SEM, phase noise, frequency error, RX sensitivity,
     blocker, intermodulation, gain/NF, calibration tables

3. PHY / waveform validation
   → Mostly non-signaling
   → Generate known waveforms, analyze demod quality, stress RF front-end behavior

4. Integration with baseband / modem / firmware
   → Start using signaling tester
   → Attach/call/session setup, protocol-controlled RF states, scheduler behavior

5. System validation / conformance / operator-like testing
   → Signaling tester
   → End-to-end behavior, RF under network control, mobility, carrier aggregation,
     power control, protocol/RF interaction

6. Production test
   → Usually non-signaling for speed/cost
   → Signaling only if final product-level functional verification is required
```

### Non-signaling tester fit

For **semiconductor RFIC validation**, the non-signaling setup is usually the main workhorse because the RFIC team needs deterministic, low-level RF control. The DUT is not necessarily running a full protocol stack. You directly force the chip into TX/RX modes and measure RF performance.

Use it for:

- TX output power, gain control, linearity
- EVM, constellation quality, modulation accuracy
- ACLR/ACPR, spectrum emission mask
- RX sensitivity, PER/BER/BLER using controlled waveforms
- blocker/desense, intermodulation, coexistence stress
- calibration and trimming
- PVT characterization: process, voltage, temperature
- regression across bands, bandwidths, MIMO paths, RF modes

In R&S context, the **R&S CMP180** is described as a radio communication tester used to verify signal waveform bandwidth in loopback mode for R&D and production, which aligns more with RF/waveform-centric non-signaling or production-style validation use cases.

### Signaling tester fit

A **signaling tester** fits once the RFIC is part of a larger platform — RFIC + baseband/modem + protocol stack + firmware — and you want to validate behavior under realistic network or access-point control.

Use it for:

- Cellular/Wi-Fi attach, registration, call/data session setup
- RF performance while the protocol stack controls the radio
- Power control and scheduling behavior
- Carrier aggregation / multi-link / MIMO behavior
- Mobility, handover, reselection, beam management
- Protocol/RF interaction bugs
- Pre-conformance and conformance-style testing

In R&S context, the **CMX500** is positioned as a **5G one-box signaling tester** and multi-technology, multi-channel signaling tester. The sourced material says it supports end-to-end signaling use cases, RF conformance, protocol validation, and R&D testing. It is also described as enabling RF TX/RX measurements under real-world signaling mode for wireless device development.

### Simple rule of thumb

| Stage | Best fit | Why |
|---|---|---|
| RFIC bring-up | Non-signaling | Direct RF control, fast debug |
| RF parameter validation | Non-signaling | Repeatable, deterministic measurements |
| Calibration / characterization | Non-signaling | High-volume sweeps over bands/PVT |
| RFIC + modem integration | Both | Non-signaling for RF debug, signaling for system behavior |
| Device/system validation | Signaling | Realistic network-controlled operation |
| Conformance/pre-certification | Signaling | Protocol + RF behavior under standards |
| Production | Mostly non-signaling | Speed, cost, automation |

So for a **semiconductor RFIC validation** use case, I would position:

- **Non-signaling tester** as the core validation platform for RFIC design verification and characterization.
- **Signaling tester** as the system/integration validation platform after the RFIC is connected to a modem/baseband and needs to prove real-world wireless behavior.

passages.text: ## Rohde & Schwarz and SmartViser have partnered to develop a solution for testing compliance with a new regulation that will require Energy Efficiency Index (EEI) labeling for smartphones and tablets sold in the EU. At the core of the solution is the R&S CMX500, a radio communication tester that supports end-to-end testing of all signaling use cases, combined with SmartViser’s viSer test automation application – available for Android and iOS. Both companies will showcase the solution at Mobile World Congress 2024.

passages.text: Rohde & Schwarz will display its [R&S CMX500](https://www.rohde-schwarz.com/us/products/test-and-measurement/wireless-tester-network-emulator/cmx500-5g-one-box-signaling-tester_63493-601282.html "CMX500") multi-technology multi-channel signaling tester at MWC 2024 with newly added Wi-Fi 7 testing capabilities. With this functionality, the one-box tester allows R&D engineers of wireless devices to comprehensively test their design’s operation in cellular and non-cellular standards of the latest generation in a single instrument setup. In addition to this, the [R&S CMP180](https://www.rohde-schwarz.com/us/products/test-and-measurement/wireless-tester-rf-analyzer-generator/cmp180-radio-communication-tester_63493-1081280.html "CMP180") radio communication tester will verify a signal waveform of 480 MHz bandwidth in loopback mode, attesting to be a future-proof solution for users in R&D and production, even beyond the requirements of Wi-Fi 7.

passages.text: At the core of this test solution is the tried and tested CMX500 5G one-box signaling tester from Rohde & Schwarz. This all-in-one test platform supports both SA and NSA architectures, covers frequency ranges from FR1 to FR3 (up to 18 GHz) and features a built-in IMS server, enabling one-stop testing for RF conformance, protocol validation, VoNR acoustics and carrier aggregation. With these capabilities, the CMX500 serves as a key test platform for 5G-Advanced and 6G research and development.

passages.text: During the development of WLAN devices, measurements of the RF TX and RX characteristics must be conducted under real-world conditions in signaling mode. The R&S CMX500 one-box tester is a multi-technology multi-channel signaling tester that is now available with integrated Wi-Fi 7 test functionality. Especially in Wi-Fi 7 where Multi-Link-Operation (MLO) is a key feature, a test environment that provides multiple RF chains is crucial. The tester's flexibility, support for multiple radio technologies, and embedded IP test capabilities make it a versatile solution for a wide range of Wi-Fi 7-specific tests, such as 2x2 MIMO, 6 GHz band with out-of-band discovery, coexistence and E2E test capabilities.

answer.text:
In the supported RAW context, a Signaling Tester fits where RF TX/RX measurements must run under real-world signaling mode, with the R&S CMX500 identified as a multi-technology, multi-channel signaling tester for such tests [8].
The CMX500 is also described as a 5G one-box signaling tester supporting end-to-end signaling use cases, RF conformance, protocol validation, and R&D use [1][2][6].
The closest R&S non-signaling-related product context is the R&S CMP180 radio communication tester, which is described as verifying a signal waveform in loopback mode for R&D and production use [5].
